questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q01

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | foundation

Which definition best describes the Cold War?

generalfeedback.text: The rivalry involved competing systems, power, alliances, propaganda, crises, and proxy conflicts.

answer.text: A temporary trade disagreement within Western Europe
A long-term political, ideological, military, and economic rivalry primarily between the United States and Soviet Union
A direct declared war fought only in Germany
A period when international conflict ended

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q02

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | foundation

What was the central purpose of the U.S. policy of containment?

generalfeedback.text: Containment initially emphasized limiting further expansion through diplomatic, economic, and military policies.

answer.text: To overthrow every existing communist government immediately
To restore European colonial empires
To limit further expansion of Soviet or communist influence
To dissolve NATO in 1949

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q03

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | foundation

Which description of the Marshall Plan is most accurate?

generalfeedback.text: The European Recovery Program had multiple purposes and should not be reduced to one motive.

answer.text: A Soviet military alliance
A U.S.-supported European recovery program with economic, humanitarian, strategic, and political purposes
A plan to divide Berlin into four sectors
A treaty creating East Germany

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q04

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | foundation

What does collective defense mean?

generalfeedback.text: Collective defense is a mutual security commitment.

answer.text: Members agree to cooperate in response to an attack on one member
Every member must have an identical government
Neutral states automatically join a military bloc
A state gives up all foreign-policy choices

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q05

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | foundation

Churchill’s phrase Iron Curtain referred to

generalfeedback.text: The phrase was a metaphor, not a single physical barrier across Europe.

answer.text: a literal metal wall crossing every European border
the Allied occupation boundary in Japan
a political metaphor for Europe’s developing East-West division
the Berlin Airlift flight path

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q06

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | interpretation

Why was West Berlin geographically vulnerable?

generalfeedback.text: West Berlin depended on access routes crossing Soviet-controlled territory.

answer.text: It was controlled by the Soviet Union but located in France
It had no civilian population
It was a Western-controlled area surrounded by the Soviet occupation zone
It was outside Germany and accessible only by sea

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q07

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | interpretation

Berlin crisis evidence
DevelopmentGeographic factResponse
Soviet blockade, 1948–1949West Berlin was surrounded by the Soviet occupation zone.Western Allies delivered food, fuel, and supplies by air until the blockade ended.

Which claim is best supported by both stimuli?

generalfeedback.text: The map and table connect Berlin’s location to blockade and airlift.

answer.text: Geography allowed the Soviet Union to restrict Western land access, while air routes enabled a Western response
The Western zones surrounded the Soviet zone
Berlin was not divided after World War II
The airlift created the Warsaw Pact in 1948

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q08

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | interpretation

Cold War origins chronology
DateDevelopment
1945Yalta and Potsdam conferences
1946Churchill’s “Iron Curtain” speech
1947Truman Doctrine and Marshall recovery proposal
1948–1949Berlin Blockade and Airlift
1949NATO; West and East Germany established
1955Warsaw Pact

Which chronological statement is accurate?

generalfeedback.text: The chronology prevents the common error of treating the alliances as simultaneous.

answer.text: The Warsaw Pact formed before the Truman Doctrine
NATO and the Warsaw Pact formed simultaneously
NATO formed in 1949, while the Warsaw Pact followed in 1955
The Berlin Airlift began after 1955

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q09

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | interpretation

Cold War origins chronology
DateDevelopment
1945Yalta and Potsdam conferences
1946Churchill’s “Iron Curtain” speech
1947Truman Doctrine and Marshall recovery proposal
1948–1949Berlin Blockade and Airlift
1949NATO; West and East Germany established
1955Warsaw Pact

Which sequence best illustrates increasing institutional division?

generalfeedback.text: The sequence traces policy, crisis, and formal alliance development.

answer.text: Warsaw Pact → Yalta → Marshall Plan
Truman Doctrine/Marshall Plan → Berlin crisis → NATO → Warsaw Pact
NATO → World War II → Potsdam
Berlin Airlift → Yalta → Iron Curtain speech

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q10

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | interpretation

Representative political-economic models
CategoryUnited States/Western modelSoviet model
Political organizationMultiparty representative governmentCommunist Party rule
Economic organizationMarket economy and private investmentState-directed economy
PropertySubstantial private ownershipExtensive state ownership/control

Qualification: Not every country in either bloc operated identically.

Which conclusion is best supported?

generalfeedback.text: The chart supports comparison while preserving variation.

answer.text: Political-economic differences existed, but countries within each bloc were not identical
All Western countries had identical constitutions
The Soviet and Western models had no meaningful differences
Every Eastern European government changed voluntarily in the same way

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q11

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | interpretation

Competing security perspectives after World War II
Soviet perspectiveWestern perspective
Devastating wartime losses; earlier invasions from the west; desire for friendly border governmentsSoviet military presence; suppression of political opposition; fear of further communist expansion
Policy emphasis: security bufferPolicy emphasis: containment

Explaining a perspective does not make all actions equivalent or justified.

What does the comparison reveal?

generalfeedback.text: Competing security perceptions contributed to a security dilemma.

answer.text: Only ideology influenced Cold War policy
Both sides described security concerns differently, and each could interpret the other’s actions as threatening
Explaining a Soviet concern excuses political repression
Western leaders welcomed Soviet expansion

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q12

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | interpretation

“From Stettin in the Baltic to Trieste in the Adriatic, an iron curtain has descended across the Continent.”

Winston Churchill, “Sinews of Peace,” March 5, 1946. UK National Archives, FO 371/51624; excerpt preserved.

Which sourcing observation is strongest?

generalfeedback.text: Creator, audience, purpose, and limitation matter when using a political speech.

answer.text: The speech provides a prominent Western interpretation and should be compared with Soviet and Eastern European evidence
The speaker represented every European citizen
The metaphor proves a literal wall existed in 1946
The speech is quantitative evidence about Marshall Plan aid

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q13

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | interpretation

“It must be the policy of the United States to support free peoples who are resisting attempted subjugation...”

President Harry S. Truman, address to Congress, March 12, 1947. U.S. Department of State; public-domain government text; omission marked.

What policy claim does the excerpt make?

generalfeedback.text: Truman publicly framed U.S. aid as support for peoples resisting coercion.

answer.text: The United States should withdraw from Greece and Turkey
The United States should support peoples portrayed as resisting subjugation
All European states should join the Warsaw Pact
Germany should remain permanently united under Soviet control

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q14

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | interpretation

“Our policy is directed not against any country or doctrine but against hunger, poverty, desperation and chaos.”

George C. Marshall, Harvard University, June 5, 1947. U.S. Department of State, FRUS 1947, vol. III, doc. 140; public-domain government text.

Which interpretation best uses the source and its context?

generalfeedback.text: The program combined humanitarian, economic, strategic, and political purposes.

answer.text: The plan had only military goals
The public statement emphasized recovery and human suffering, while historians should also assess economic and strategic purposes
The statement proves the Soviet Union wrote the plan
The recovery proposal ended all political rivalry

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q15

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | interpretation

“It must be the policy of the United States to support free peoples who are resisting attempted subjugation...”

President Harry S. Truman, address to Congress, March 12, 1947. U.S. Department of State; public-domain government text; omission marked.

“Our policy is directed not against any country or doctrine but against hunger, poverty, desperation and chaos.”

George C. Marshall, Harvard University, June 5, 1947. U.S. Department of State, FRUS 1947, vol. III, doc. 140; public-domain government text.

How do the two sources differ in emphasis?

generalfeedback.text: The sources support different but overlapping dimensions of containment.

answer.text: Truman emphasizes resistance to political subjugation; Marshall emphasizes economic breakdown and recovery
Marshall calls for the Warsaw Pact; Truman calls for NATO
Both reject any U.S. role in Europe
Both discuss only Berlin’s air routes

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q16

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | application

Which explanation best avoids reducing the Cold War to capitalism versus communism?

generalfeedback.text: Strong causal reasoning weighs interacting conditions and decisions.

answer.text: The rivalry resulted only from economic vocabulary
Ideology interacted with security fears, postwar power, geography, competing influence, and political decisions
The Berlin crisis had no connection to geography
One speech created the rivalry by itself

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q17

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | application

Competing security perspectives after World War II
Soviet perspectiveWestern perspective
Devastating wartime losses; earlier invasions from the west; desire for friendly border governmentsSoviet military presence; suppression of political opposition; fear of further communist expansion
Policy emphasis: security bufferPolicy emphasis: containment

Explaining a perspective does not make all actions equivalent or justified.

Which situation best illustrates a security dilemma?

generalfeedback.text: A security dilemma occurs when defensive measures appear threatening and provoke escalation.

answer.text: One side’s defensive buffer appears expansionist to the other, whose response then increases the first side’s fear
Both sides agree that no security measures are needed
A neutral country changes its currency
Every state interprets the same policy identically

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q18

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | application

Which claim-evidence-reasoning statement is strongest?

generalfeedback.text: The strongest CER connects a precise map detail to blockade and response.

answer.text: Claim: Berlin mattered. Evidence: It had buildings. Reasoning: All cities cause alliances.
Claim: Geography intensified the crisis. Evidence: West Berlin was surrounded by the Soviet zone. Reasoning: Soviet control of land routes made blockade possible and encouraged an airlift response.
Claim: Berlin created communism. Evidence: It was in Germany. Reasoning: Maps prove ideology.
Claim: Geography was irrelevant. Evidence: Four zones existed. Reasoning: Location never shapes policy.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q19

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | application

Which pair is the clearest early Cold War action-response cycle?

generalfeedback.text: The blockade and airlift form a direct, geographically grounded action-response relationship.

answer.text: Berlin Blockade → Berlin Airlift
Yalta → World War II begins
Warsaw Pact → NATO dissolves
Marshall Plan → Germany is defeated

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q20

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | application

A student explains that Soviet leaders wanted friendly border states after devastating invasions. What must the student add to avoid an inaccurate conclusion?

generalfeedback.text: Perspective analysis explains motives without endorsing actions or erasing variation.

answer.text: Security concerns automatically justified suppression of opposition
Understanding the concern does not excuse coercion, and conditions varied across Eastern Europe
Every Eastern European state freely chose identical institutions
Western governments had no security concerns

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q21

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | application

Which conclusion about Yalta and Potsdam uses sound causation?

generalfeedback.text: No single conference fully explains the Cold War’s emergence.

answer.text: One conference alone started the Cold War
The conferences addressed postwar problems and exposed disagreements, but the rivalry developed through multiple conditions and later decisions
The conferences created NATO and the Warsaw Pact simultaneously
They ended disagreement over Poland and Germany

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q22

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | application

“Our policy is directed not against any country or doctrine but against hunger, poverty, desperation and chaos.”

George C. Marshall, Harvard University, June 5, 1947. U.S. Department of State, FRUS 1947, vol. III, doc. 140; public-domain government text.

A historian argues that the Marshall Plan was purely humanitarian. Which evaluation is strongest?

generalfeedback.text: Historical evaluation distinguishes public emphasis from multiple purposes and effects.

answer.text: Accept the claim because public speeches reveal every motive
Reject all humanitarian effects
Revise the claim: recovery and human need mattered, but economic stability and containment also shaped the program
Conclude that the plan was a Soviet policy

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q23

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | application

Which thesis best supports an evidence-based investigation of responsibility for the early Cold War?

generalfeedback.text: A defensible thesis weighs competing interpretations without creating false equivalence.

answer.text: Only one side acted, so no comparison is necessary
Responsibility should be evaluated through Soviet expansion and security policies, U.S. containment and economic power, mutual mistrust, ideology, and the postwar power vacuum
Neither side made political decisions
A single leader’s speech determined every later event

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q24

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | application

Why is it inaccurate to describe Europe as two perfectly homogeneous camps?

generalfeedback.text: Bloc labels are useful, but they do not erase national variation or nonalignment.

answer.text: NATO never existed
States within and outside the blocs had different political conditions, interests, and degrees of independence, including neutral and nonaligned states
East and West Germany were the same state after 1949
The Warsaw Pact began in 1945

questiontext.text:
Question ID: WH_U06_L01_Q25

Alignment: MLA.WH.CW.01–02 | application

Cold War origins chronology
DateDevelopment
1945Yalta and Potsdam conferences
1946Churchill’s “Iron Curtain” speech
1947Truman Doctrine and Marshall recovery proposal
1948–1949Berlin Blockade and Airlift
1949NATO; West and East Germany established
1955Warsaw Pact

Which conclusion best explains how rivalry divided Europe?

generalfeedback.text: The conclusion integrates cause, chronology, geography, and institutional change.

answer.text: Ideology automatically divided every country in 1945
Postwar disputes and competing security policies produced actions and responses; Berlin became a geographic flashpoint, while German division and alliances institutionalized the rivalry
The airlift ended all Cold War competition
The Warsaw Pact caused the 1946 speech
